**The Weight of Small Moments**

I remember the first time I saw the ocean. It wasn’t a grand, sweeping view—just a narrow strip of blue between the sand and the horizon, the kind of sea you’d see from a pier or a beachside café. But even then, it felt vast, impossible to measure. The water moved in slow, rhythmic waves, and the air smelled of salt and something else—something like the distant hum of the world.

That day, I didn’t understand how much the ocean would come to mean to me. But over time, I learned that the sea isn’t just water; it’s memory. It’s the way the tide rolls in and out, carrying secrets and leaving them behind. It’s the way the sun sets over it, painting the sky in gold and pink, and the way the waves sometimes crash with a sound like a whisper or a scream.

I’ve stood on beaches where the sand was warm and the air was thick with the scent of jasmine, and I’ve walked through cities where the streets were crowded and the air was heavy with the weight of too many voices. The ocean, in its quiet way, reminds me that some things are worth waiting for—the way the tide will always come back, no matter how long you’ve been gone.

And sometimes, when I’m standing on the shore, watching the waves lap at the rocks, I wonder if the sea knows the weight of small moments. The way a single word can change everything. The way a glance can mean more than a thousand words. The way a moment of stillness, just standing there, can feel like an eternity.

The ocean doesn’t rush. It doesn’t need to. It just is, patient and endless, carrying everything forward. And in that, I think it’s the most beautiful thing of all.
